signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5766, supported by a strong G10 outperformance theme where AUD averages +1.035% across its peer group. The pair is underpinned by a substantial +435bp carry advantage as RBA 4.35% is paired with SNB 0.00%, creating a high-conviction carry environment while VIX remains at 15.4. AUD positioning is increasingly crowded with LF net at +49,749 (94th percentile), yet retail sentiment is 90% short, providing a contrarian fuel for further upside. AUD/USD technicals show the currency cluster well above the SMA20/50/200, confirming broad-based momentum. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage and retail divergence favor trend extension. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep for regional cross-proxy sentiment. Risk: VIX spikes above 25, triggering a sharp unwind of the crowded AUD long position.

signals.title: EUR/JPY — ECB Repricing + Options Skew
signals.text: EUR/JPY trades at 185.52, with the Euro finding fresh support from TIER-1 reports that the ECB is set for a September rate hike. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Institutional options markets signal caution as the 25d risk reversal at -1.66 reflects a strong put skew, indicating that desks are paying for protection against a JPY snapback. This divergence between hawkish ECB headlines and heavy options hedging suggests a volatile consolidation phase near recent highs. Trade bias: Long EUR/JPY; hawkish ECB policy shift supports carry while hedging demand limits chase. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: BoJ verbal intervention triggers a sharp correction toward the SMA200 at 158.36.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Trade Tension + Oil Contagion
signals.text: USD/CAD at 1.3862 is reversing earlier gains as TIER-1 headlines report widening US tariffs on Canada alongside a -2.45% drop in WTI oil prices to $80.3. The CAD ESI remains strong at +23.4, but this macro resilience is being tested by deteriorating trade relations and a negative -0.281 correlation with oil. Despite these headwinds, USD/CAD remains technically weak, trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3926, 1.4055, and 1.3841 respectively. Speculative positioning is heavily short CAD at -89,836 (3rd percentile), creating a high-risk environment for a short-squeeze if trade tensions de-escalate. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by trade friction and falling crude prices. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Crude oil recovers above $85, invalidating the CAD weakness thesis.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Risk Premium Extreme
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3638 continues to hold its bullish technical posture above the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.3520/1.3404. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk with an implied volatility of 11.0% against a realized HV30 of only 5.8%, resulting in an extreme +5.2% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP). This suggests institutional traders are aggressively buying protection despite a neutral 25d risk reversal of -0.09 and a crowded spec long position (92nd percentile). The high cost of protection relative to actual movement indicates market participants are bracing for a volatility spike that has yet to manifest in spot prices. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated VRP makes long entries expensive. Catalyst: US PCE data 28 Aug. Risk: GBP/USD closes below the SMA20 at 1.3520, confirming a shift from consolidation to correction.
